newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-JONES OPENS EUROPEAN CAMPAIGN WITH A WIN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES OPENS EUROPEAN CAMPAIGN WITH A WIN.

text.p: American Marion Jones, who has recorded the year's three fastest 100 metres times, marked her European debut with a comfortable victory at an event in Turin on Tuesday.
Jones, winner of the long jump at the recent U.S. championships, won in a wind-assisted 11.08 seconds, easing off as she neared the line.
Russian Natalya Voronova was second in 11.29 and Alenka Bikar from Slovenia third in 11.36.
Jones, 21, is scheduled to run again in Lille, France, on Sunday, in Lausanne on July 2 and Oslo on July 4.
She is then scheduled to compete in the 200 metres in Stockholm on July 7 before bidding for gold in her three specialist events at August's world championships in Athens.
Italian world champion Fiona May built on her success in last week's European Cup final in Munich by recording a season's best 6.97 metres to win the long jump.
The British-born Olympic silver medallist beat Russians Ludmila Galkina (6.80) and Ludmila Ninova (6.70) into second and third places respectively.
There was a season's best in the men's long jump, with Jamaican Olympic silver medallist James Beckford jumping 8.49 metres.
Dennis Mitchell won the men's 100 metres in 10.20 seconds, Uganda's Atlanta bronze medallist Davis Kamoga triumphed in the 400 metres and Zambia's Samuel Matete won the 400 hurdles.
